chunks: 1305 - And Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a woman who was on the way to Mecca and performed the Maghrib salat, going and returning, as two rakʿahs and two rakʿahs. So he said: "There is no repeat upon her."
And in the narration of al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, he said:

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّل: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the Imam answering the legal question
key_terms.إِعَادَةٌ: repetition of the prayer within its time
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the Maghrib salat, the sunset prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs, indicating the shortened form mentioned in the case
key_terms.طَرِيقِ مَكَّةَ: the route to Mecca, indicating travel context
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: makeup performance of the prayer after its time

ai.seo_question: Does a traveler who mistakenly prays Maghrib as two rakʿahs have to repeat or make it up?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman traveler who performed Maghrib salat incorrectly as two rakʿahs while going and returning on the road to Mecca. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام states that she is not required to repeat the prayer, and another narration clarifies that no makeup prayer is due upon her.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1305 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr reported from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (as) about a woman who was on the way to Mecca and performed the Maghrib prayer two rak'ahs going and two rak'ahs returning.
Imam (as) said: "She does not need to repeat it."
In another narration from al-Hussain ibn Sa'id, from ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (as), Imam (as) said:
"There is no obligation to make it up."
